clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-547 on Robinhood Chain: a mined transaction in which an unlock frame reverted and a later unlock of the same transaction succeeded.
clearedSpotChecks.note: eth_getTransactionReceipt for 0x222fe1797dd7dcfd16c424c6d6abc0fd48c589c5194ea44ad7184fc932a73e10 on https://rpc.mainnet.chain.robinhood.com, run in this session, returns status 0x1 in block 122,127,614 with two logs from the PoolManager 0x8366a39c... under topic 0x40e9cecb... (Swap). Walking l547_hit_trace.json gives three calls with selector 0x48c89491 (unlock) to the PoolManager: the first from 0x8f10b468... succeeds, the second from 0x1caddfdb... ends with execution reverted after a swap call, and the third from 0x8f10b468... succeeds. PoolManager.unlock reverts with AlreadyUnlocked when the flag is set (src/PoolManager.sol:104-105), the flag is written with tstore (src/libraries/Lock.sol:10-15) and cleared only after the callback (src/PoolManager.sol:111-113). A kept flag from the reverted frame would have made the third unlock revert, so the mined block rolled the transient write back. The trace is a replay by an RPC node, but the mined receipt, with status 1 and two Swap logs, stands on its own.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Lead L-577: the arithmetic, comparison, shift, BYTE, SIGNEXTEND, EXP, KECCAK256, CALLDATALOAD, MLOAD, MSTORE, MCOPY, PUSH, DUP and SWAP implementations and their jump table entries at fork commit 0e44603, read against the specification.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read core/vm/instructions.go and core/vm/stack.go at 0e44603 and uint256.go at v1.3.2. pop1Peek1 returns the old top first and the new top second (stack.go lines 165 to 169) and pop2Peek1 returns top, second and the new top (lines 174 to 178), so DIV, SDIV, MOD, SMOD, SUB and EXP write op(a, b) for top a and second b, ADDMOD and MULMOD write (a op b) mod N into the third slot, SIGNEXTEND calls ExtendSign(x, b) and BYTE calls x.Byte(i) (instructions.go lines 34 to 86, 172 to 188). SHL and SHR clear for a shift of 256 or more (lines 195 to 219). SAR sends shifts above 256 to the sign fill branch and a shift of exactly 256 to SRsh, which returns all ones for a negative value at n >= 256 (uint256.go lines 1110 to 1121) and Rsh, which returns zero for n = 256 through rsh192 and a Go shift of 64 (lines 1075 to 1083). JUMPI tests the full word with IsZero before validJumpdest (instructions.go lines 540 to 552). This matches the specification for the operations used at src/libraries/FullMath.sol, src/libraries/TickMath.sol, src/libraries/BitMath.sol and src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Stack arena and pooled memory introduced in the fork interpreter: can a nested call, a Stylus program calling back into the EVM, or a pooled buffer change a value the PoolManager computed or the return data it reads.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Read stack.go, memory.go, interpreter.go and instructions.go at 0e44603. A child stack starts at the arena top and the arena grows with slices.Grow when fewer than 1,024 slots remain (stack.go lines 56 to 70); a Stack holds a pointer to the arena and indexes s.inner.data on every access (lines 100 to 112), so a parent push after a growth writes into the new backing array. opCall, opCallCode, opDelegateCall and opStaticCall pop every argument with pop(), which returns a value copy (stack.go lines 114 to 118), and push the success word through stack.push after evm.Call returns (instructions.go lines 725 to 885). RETURN and REVERT hand back GetCopy slices (lines 887 to 905), so the return data buffer never aliases a child memory that Free clears and returns to the pool (memory.go lines 43 to 52, interpreter.go lines 125 and 149 to 150). Free clears the buffer up to its length and Resize only reslices within capacity, so bytes a frame sees past its previous size are zero. Input to a child is a GetPtr slice of the caller memory, as on Ethereum, and the caller does not run while the child runs.
